opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and sports marketing — up 15%, primarily on higher sports and brand marketing.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Salaries, technology and running the business — down 3%, as the year-ago quarter carried restructuring charges.

footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($9M) and Corporate (-$23M, mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: down 440 basis points, on discounts and channel mix

oneTimers: The effective tax rate was 33.6%, versus 13.1% a year ago — Nike said lower stock-compensation benefits and one-time items had an outsized impact because pre-tax income was so small.
otherDetail: $22M of net interest income, less $25M of other expense, net.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — footwear fell 13% and apparel 7%; equipment rose 1%.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Europe, the Middle East and Africa — down 9% on reported numbers, down 10% without currency help.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Asia-Pacific (outside Greater China) and Latin America — down 8% reported, down 3% without currency help.

segments.name: Greater China
segments.note: China — the weakest region this quarter, with footwear down 21%.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Converse sneaker brand — down across all territories.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global brand divisions plus corporate leftovers (mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.

takeaways.text: Revenue fell 12% to $11.1B (down 11% without currency effects). Nike Direct fell 14% as digital sales dropped 26%, wholesale fell 9%, and every geography declined — Greater China most, at −21%.
takeaways.title: Sales fell everywhere

takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 440 basis points to 40.3%, primarily on higher discounts and changes in channel mix, as Nike cleared inventory to make room for new product. Inventories ended flat at $7.5B.
takeaways.title: Discounts squeezed the margin

takeaways.text: Net income fell 86% to $211M and EPS to $0.14. Management called the quarter the largest financial impact from its 'Win Now' actions and said the headwinds should moderate from here.
takeaways.title: Profit fell 86%

verdict: Nike's revenue fell 12% to $11.1B and profit dropped 86% to $211M — the quarter management called the largest financial hit from its 'Win Now' reset, with discounts cutting the gross margin by more than four points.
